questions.question: A sum of Rs. 12,000 amounts to Rs. 15,972 at a certain rate percent per annum in 1(1)/(2) years, when the interest is compounded half-yearly, What will be the amount of the same sum in same time and with the same rate, if interest is compounded annually?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Amount to Principal = 15972 ÷ 12000 = 1331/1000 = (11/10)³.

Since time is 3 half-years, compounding factor = 1.1 ⇒ half-yearly rate = 10%.

Annual rate = 10% × 2 = 20%.

For 1.5 years compounded annually, effective multiplying factor = 1.20 (for 1st year) × 1.10 (for 0.5 year) = 1.32.

New Amount = 12000 × 1.32 = 15840.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 15,840.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 12,000

Amount (A) after 1.5 years = Rs. 15,972 (compounded half-yearly)

Time = 1.5 years = 3 half-years

**Formula Used:**

Compound Amount, A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the annual rate of interest be R%.

⇒ For half-yearly compounding, rate = R/2 % and time = 3 periods.

⇒ 15972 = 12000 × (1 + R/200)³

⇒ (1 + R/200)³ = 15972 ÷ 12000

⇒ (1 + R/200)³ = 1331 ÷ 1000

⇒ 1 + R/200 = 11/10

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate of interest is halved (R/2) and the time period is doubled (2T).

Fractional Year Compounding

If time is given in fractions like t = n + a/b years, the formula used is: Amount = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ × (1 + (a/b × R)/100).

Simple vs Compound Interest Difference

For the first year, both Simple Interest and Compound Interest are exactly the same. The difference arises from the second period onwards as interest is calculated on accumulated interest.

questions.question: A 6 cm long chord subtends an angle of 60° at the center of the circle. If the length of another chord of the same circle is 6√3 cm, then find the measure of the angle subtended by the chord at the center of the circle.

If a chord subtends 60° at the center, the triangle formed is equilateral → Radius (r) = Chord = 6 cm.

Use Chord formula: Length = 2 × r × sin(θ/2)

6√3 = 2 × 6 × sin(θ/2) ⇒ sin(θ/2) = √3 / 2

Since sin(60°) = √3 / 2, then θ/2 = 60° ⇒ θ = 120°.

**∴ The correct answer is 120°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of chord = 2 × r × sin(θ/2)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 6 = 2 × r × sin(30°)

⇒ 6 = 2 × r × (1/2) ⇒ r = 6 cm

⇒ For Chord 2: 6√3 = 2 × 6 × sin(θ₂/2)

⇒ 6√3 = 12 × sin(θ₂/2)

⇒ θ₂/2 = sin−¹(√3/2) = 60°

Chord Length Formula

The length of a chord subtending an angle θ at the center of a circle with radius r is given by L = 2r sin(θ/2).

Equilateral Triangle Property

A chord that subtends a 60° angle at the center always forms an equilateral triangle with the two radii, meaning the chord length equals the radius.

Angle Subtended at Circumference

The angle subtended by a chord at the center is exactly twice the angle subtended by it at any point on the major arc of the circumference.</p

questions.question: Punit goes from his home to his relative's place at a speed of 45 km/h. While returning from the relative's place, due to traffic, it takes him an hour longer as he can only drive at the speed of 40 km/h. Find the distance (in km) of his relative's place from his home.
questions.solution:

Distance = Speed x Time (when speed and time are constant)

**Calculation:**

Let's assume the distance between Punit's home and his relative's place to be 'd' km.

Then, the time taken while going would be:

Time = Distance / Speed = d / 45

While returning, the time taken would be:

Time = Distance / Speed = d / 40

As given, the time taken while returning is 1 hour more than the time taken while going:

d / 40 - d / 45 = 1

Simplifying the above equation, we get:

d = 360 km

**Therefore, the distance of Punit's relative's place from his home is 360 km.**

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding the Magnification is correct?

I. A negative sign in the value of the magnification indicates that the image is real.

II. A positive sign in the value of the magnification indicates that the image is virtual.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Magnification** is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object.
 
• A **negative sign** in magnification indicates that the image is **real and inverted**.
 
• A **positive sign** in magnification indicates that the image is **virtual and upright**.
 
• Real images are formed when light rays converge, while virtual images are formed when light rays appear to diverge.
 
• The formula for magnification is given as **m = -v/u**, where 'v' is the image distance and 'u' is the object distance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Real Image:** A real image is formed when light rays actually converge at a point. It is inverted and can be projected onto a screen.
 
• **Virtual Image:** A virtual image is formed when light rays appear to diverge from a point. It is upright and cannot be projected onto a screen.
 
• **Convex Lens:** A convex lens can produce both real and virtual images depending on the position of the object relative to the focal point.
 
• **Concave Lens:** A concave lens always forms virtual, upright, and diminished images regardless of the object's position.
 
• The concept of magnification is widely used in optics, such as in microscopes, telescopes, and cameras, to study or capture images at different scales.

The correct answer is __**Transmitting sensory information from receptors to the central nervous system**__.

__
 
• **Afferent neurons**, also known as sensory neurons, are part of the peripheral nervous system responsible for carrying **sensory information** to the central nervous system (CNS).
 
• These neurons transmit data from **sensory receptors** located in tissues, organs, and skin to the brain and spinal cord.
 
• The information carried by afferent neurons includes stimuli such as **touch, pain, temperature, and body position**.
 
• Afferent neurons play a critical role in enabling the CNS to process external and internal environmental changes.

questions.question: With respect to TCP/IP, what is the full form of TFTP?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Trivial File Transfer Protocol**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The full form of the **TCP/IP** is** Transmission Control Protocol/ Internet Protocol**. 
 
• The full form of **TFTP** is **Trivial File Transfer Protocol. **
 
• It is mainly used for allowing a client to put or fetch a file from the remote host.
 
• TFTP is easy to install in a local area network system.

**Thus the correct answer is the ***Trivial File Transfer Protocol*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Discussing the other layers of the TCP/IP layers below:

 
• **Physical layer: **The first layer of the OSI model builds the physical connection between the devices. The information is divided into small bits and then transfer from one device to another.
 
• **Data link layer:** This layer is the second layer of the OSI model. Here, data is transferred from node to node.
 
• **Internet layer: **This layer is the third layer of the TCP model. It transfers the data frame from one host of a network to another host of another network. The Internet layer includes the powerful Internet Protocol (IP), the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP), and the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP).
 
• **Transport layer: **This layer is the fourth layer of the OSI model. This layer uses TCP\IP and UDP protocols for transmitting the data.
 
• **Application layer: **This layer is the seventh layer or the top layer of the OSI model. In this layer, humans can interact with the system through different applications and are also able to connect with the network. High-level protocols are used in this layer for managing data transmission and networking.

 

The **OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) **model is a conceptual framework used to understand and implement computer networking protocols in seven distinct layers. Each layer has specific functions and communicates with the layers directly above and below it. Here is a brief definition and some important information about each layer:

 
• **Physical Layer (Layer 1)**

 
 
• Definition: This layer is concerned with the transmission of raw bit streams over a physical medium.
 
• Important Information: It deals with hardware elements (such as switches, cables, and network adapters), electrical signals, and physical data rates. It defines the means of sending and receiving data bits across a network.
 
 
 
• **Data Link Layer (Layer 2)**
 
 
• Definition: This layer provides node-to-node data transfer—a link between two directly connected nodes.
 
• Important Information: It handles error detection and correction from the physical layer, frame synchronization, and flow control. The Data Link Layer is divided into two sublayers: the Media Access Control (MAC) layer and the Logical Link Control (LLC) layer.
 
 
 
• **Network Layer (Layer 3)**
 
 
• Definition: This layer is responsible for packet forwarding including routing through different routers.
 
• Important Information: It handles logical addressing (IP addresses), routing, and path determination. Protocols like IP (Internet Protocol), ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol), and ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) operate at this layer.
 
 
 
• **Transport Layer (Layer 4)**
 
 
• Definition: This layer provides reliable data transfer services to the upper layers.
 
• Important Information: It ensures complete data transfer, error recovery, and flow control. Two main protocols in this layer are TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) and UDP (User Datagram Protocol).
 
 
 
• **Session Layer (Layer 5)**
 
 
• Definition: This layer establishes, manages, and terminates connections between applications.
 
• Important Information: It handles session setup, coordination, and termination between networked devices. It is responsible for dialog control and synchronization.
 
 
 
• **Presentation Layer (Layer 6)**
 
 
• Definition: This layer translates data between the application layer and the network format.
 
• Important Information: It handles data encryption, decryption, data compression, and data translation. This layer ensures that data is in a usable format and is encoded and decoded properly.
 
 
 
• **Application Layer (Layer 7)**
 
 
• Definition: This layer provides network services directly to the user's software applications.
 
• Important Information: It handles application services for file transfers, email, and other network software services. Protocols at this layer include HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol), FTP (File Transfer Protocol), SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol), and DNS (Domain Name System).

__
 
• **The ZigBee is a standard for addressing the need for low-cost implementation of low-power devices with fewer data rates for short-range (up to 100m) wireless communication.**
 
• It is a Personal Area Network (PAN) designed for controlling and sensing the network.

• In Star topology, all the nodes are directly connected to a centralized hub or root node which acts as a switch between the nodes.

 
 
• It consists of a coordinator and several end devices and these devices communicate only with the coordinator.
 
 
 
• **In Tree topology, all the nodes are directly or indirectly connected to the main bus or hub**.
 
 
• It consists of a central node and routers which are used to extend the network coverage.
 
 
 
• In Mesh topology, every node is interconnected to all other nodes directly.
 
 
• It provides reliability because if one node fails, the data will pass through other nodes.
 
 
 
• **The Bus topology is the simplest of all which consists of a bus or a channel that is used for communication in the network**.
